# Introduction

This file is used to conduct basic correlation analysis on recreational fishers in the 2025 SELTMP data.
Spearman correlation matrice between items in Question 8 (the frequency of recreational fishing) and Questions 14, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 24, 29, 35.  

The output includes one item-by-frequency matrix for each question, a table of the strongest correlations, and an Excel file containing the correlation, p-value, and sample-size matrices. 

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# R Setup & housekeeping
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  include = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

rm(list = ls())
objects()
```

```{r}
# Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(here)
# Hmisc (rcorr) and writexl are called with :: so they don't mask tidyverse functions
```

```{r}
# Settings
show_frequency_plots <- TRUE  # TRUE prints all question-by-frequency matrices
out_dir <- here::here("Output")
dir.create(file.path(out_dir, "heatmaps"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# 1. Prepare data

```{r}
# Import Raw Data sheet and the variable dictionary
data_file <- here::here("Data/SELTMP-2025-GBR-surveydataset_v1-0_RecFishingCLUSTERS_RyanW-Nov-3-2026.xlsx")

raw_data <- read_excel(data_file, sheet = "Raw_Data")
var_info <- read_excel(data_file, sheet = "Variable Information")

#glimpse(raw_data)
```

```{r}
# Filter data for only Rec Fishers
fisher_data <- raw_data |>
  filter(Are_you_a_Rec_Fisher == 1)

nrow(fisher_data)
```

# Select variables and set all as numeric

```{r}
# Find the variables belonging to each question using the "Variable Information" sheet
questions <- c(14, 19, 21, 23, 35, 29, 17, 15, 24)

q_vars <- map(questions, \(q) {
  var_info |>
    filter(str_detect(Variable, paste0("^q", q, "_"))) |>
    mutate(num = as.integer(str_extract(Variable, "\\d+$"))) |>
    arrange(num) |>
    pull(`Variable short name`) |>
    intersect(names(raw_data))  # drops items that are not in Raw_Data
}) |>
  set_names(paste0("Q", questions))

# Fishing-frequency variables
frequency_vars <- c("rec_fishingoffshore", "rec_fishingonshore")

# Check that the fishing-frequency variables are present in Raw_Data
missing_frequency_vars <- setdiff(frequency_vars, names(raw_data))
if (length(missing_frequency_vars) > 0) {
  stop(
    "These fishing-frequency variables were not found in Raw_Data: ",
    paste(missing_frequency_vars, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Lookup table: variable -> question -> question text
var_key <- tibble(
  variable = unlist(q_vars, use.names = FALSE),
  question = rep(names(q_vars), lengths(q_vars))
) |>
  left_join(
    var_info |> select(variable = `Variable short name`, label = Label),
    by = "variable"
  )

# Add the fishing-frequency variables to the lookup table
frequency_key <- tibble(
  variable = frequency_vars,
  question = "Fishing frequency"
) |>
  left_join(
    var_info |> select(variable = `Variable short name`, label = Label),
    by = "variable"
  )

var_key <- bind_rows(var_key, frequency_key)

lengths(q_vars)  # number of items per question
```

```{r}
# Numeric data frame used for all correlations
vars <- c(unlist(q_vars, use.names = FALSE), frequency_vars)

fisher_num <- fisher_data |>
  select(all_of(vars)) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), \(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))))

# Respondents available per item (correlations use pairwise deletion)
summary(colSums(!is.na(fisher_num)))
```

# 2. Calculate correlation matrices

```{r}
# Spearman matrix: r, p, n
run_cor <- function(data) {
  Hmisc::rcorr(as.matrix(data), type = "spearman")  # pairwise deletion
}

# Convert the matrices to one long table (one row per pair of variables)
make_long <- function(res) {
  mat_long <- function(m, nm) {
    as.data.frame(as.table(m), responseName = nm, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }

  mat_long(res$r, "r") |>
    left_join(mat_long(res$P, "p"), by = c("Var1", "Var2")) |>
    left_join(mat_long(res$n, "n"), by = c("Var1", "Var2")) |>
    rename(var1 = Var1, var2 = Var2) |>
    mutate(method = "Spearman")
}

results <- run_cor(fisher_num)

# Keep only question-item by fishing-frequency correlations
cor_all <- make_long(results) |>
  filter(var1 %in% unlist(q_vars, use.names = FALSE),
         var2 %in% frequency_vars) |>
  left_join(
    var_key |> select(var1 = variable, q1 = question),
    by = "var1"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    var_key |> select(var2 = variable, q2 = question),
    by = "var2"
  )
```

```{r}
# Heatmap function: Spearman correlations between question items and frequency variables
plot_cor <- function(rows, cols = frequency_vars, title = NULL, labels = TRUE) {
  d <- cor_all |>
    filter(var1 %in% rows, var2 %in% cols) |>
    mutate(
      sig_star = case_when(
        is.na(p) ~ "",
        p < 0.01 ~ "**",
        p < 0.05 ~ "*",
        TRUE ~ ""
      ),
      label = if_else(is.na(r), "", paste0(sprintf("%.2f", r), sig_star)),
      var1 = factor(var1, levels = rev(rows)),
      var2 = factor(var2, levels = cols)
    )

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(var2, var1, fill = r)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "#B2182B",
      mid = "white",
      high = "#2166AC",
      midpoint = 0,
      limits = c(-1, 1),
      na.value = "grey90",
      name = "r"
    ) +
    coord_fixed() +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL,
      caption = "* = p < 0.05; ** = p < 0.01 (unadjusted)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )

  if (labels) p <- p + geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.3)
  p
}
```

# 3. Question-by-frequency matrices

One matrix per question, with question items down the side and fishing-frequency variables across the top. All plots are saved to `Output/heatmaps/`.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

for (q in names(q_vars)) {
  p <- plot_cor(
    q_vars[[q]],
    title = paste(q, "vs fishing frequency")
  )

  ggsave(
    file.path(out_dir, "heatmaps", paste0(q, "_fishing_frequency.png")),
    p,
    width = 8,
    height = max(3, 2.5 + 0.4 * length(q_vars[[q]])),
    limitsize = FALSE
  )

  if (show_frequency_plots) print(p)
}
```

## Strongest correlations with fishing frequency

Top 25 item pairs with raw p-values below 0.05.

```{r}
top_pairs <- cor_all |>
  filter(!is.na(p), p < 0.05) |>
  slice_max(abs(r), n = 25) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(r))) |>
  select(method, var1, q1, var2, q2, r, p, n)

knitr::kable(top_pairs, digits = 3)
```

# 4. Export results to Excel

```{r}
mat_sheet <- function(m) as_tibble(m, rownames = "variable")

writexl::write_xlsx(
  list(
    Variable_key = var_key,
    Spearman_r = mat_sheet(
      results$r[unlist(q_vars, use.names = FALSE), frequency_vars, drop = FALSE]
    ),
    Spearman_p = mat_sheet(
      results$P[unlist(q_vars, use.names = FALSE), frequency_vars, drop = FALSE]
    ),
    Spearman_n = mat_sheet(
      results$n[unlist(q_vars, use.names = FALSE), frequency_vars, drop = FALSE]
    ),
    All_pairs = cor_all |>
      select(method, var1, q1, var2, q2, r, p, n)
  ),
  path = file.path(out_dir, "Fishing_frequency_correlations.xlsx")
)
```

# Notes on interpretation

- Spearman's correlation is used because the question responses and fishing-frequency measures are ordinal.
- Each item pair uses every respondent who answered both items (pairwise deletion), so the sample size varies between pairs.
- P-values and significance stars are unadjusted. Because many item pairs are tested, some p-values below 0.05 may occur by chance.
- A positive correlation means higher responses to a question item tend to be associated with more frequent fishing; a negative correlation means they tend to be associated with less frequent fishing. Consider each item's wording when interpreting direction.
